newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's 10-month crude oil imports up 14 pct.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's 10-month crude oil imports up 14 pct.

text.p: South Korea's crude oil imports rose 14 percent to 583.1 million barrels in the first 10 months of this year from 511.4 million barrels the year before, the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy said on Friday.
A ministry statement attributed the increase to an expansion by Hyundai Oil Refinery Co. Hyundai's new 200,000 barrels per day (bpd) crude distillation unit began operation in May.
Local oil refiners paid an average unit price of US $19.40 per barrel in January to October, on an FOB basis, up from $17.46 a year earlier.
South Korea bought 68.1 percent of its crude oil imports on a long-term contract basis and 31.9 percent in the spot market.
Middle East nations continue to be South Korea's major crude suppliers, providing about 78.1 percent of total imports in the first 10 months.
Southeast Asian countries supplied 13.1 percent, while the Americas and Africa provided the rest.
